The main takeaway from our work is that
repeated exposure to cocaine enhances the effects of corticotropin releasing factor (CRF), a stress-related neuropeptide, on excitatory transmission in dopamine neurons.

chronic cocaine exposure can enhance the ability of CRF to potentiate excitatory neurotransmission in VTA dopamine neurons, and that this effect could be a key mechanism for the enhanced vulnerability of cocaine-exposed individuals to stress-induced relapse.
